findings.title: Reflected XSS via HTML Entity Encoding Bypass
findings.description: The 'name' parameter on /page is reflected in the HTML response without proper encoding. A tag-based filter blocks direct HTML tags, but HTML entity encoding (e.g., <script>) bypasses the filter entirely, allowing arbitrary JavaScript execution. The X-XSS-Protection header is set to 0, disabling browser XSS protection.

reproduction.expected: Server responds with success umbrella and 'Let the game begin. Good Luck' message, confirming XSS filter bypass. When executed in a browser, alert('XSS') triggers and reveals the flag.

findings.title: Reflected XSS via Registration Name Field (SSTI + XSS)
findings.description: The registration step 1 name field is vulnerable to both SSTI (Server-Side Template Injection) and reflected XSS. The name is stored in the session and reflected in a <script> tag on step 3 without proper escaping. Additionally, the name is evaluated as a Django template variable on step 1, allowing SSTI attacks.
findings.evidence: Payload: "); alert(1); // renders as: alert("Hello "); alert(1); //. Just Now up to 50% OFF "). SSTI test: {% if name == flag %}MATCH{% endif %} returned MATCH, confirming flag variable exists in template context.

reproduction.command: POST /accounts/register/step1/ with name="); alert(1); // and complete registration flow through step 3
reproduction.expected: Script tag on step 3 renders: alert("Hello "); alert(1); //. Just Now up to 50% OFF ")
